case_name: Flare-On 12 (2025) — CTF Malware Reverse Engineering Corpus
description: Flare-On 12 (2025) challenge corpus. Nine CTF reversing challenges distributed as a single ZIP (1,068,300,687 bytes) containing 7z archives protected with CTF passwords. The corpus spans: disk image analysis (DrillBabyDrill), project chimera (multi-stage chain), file format RE (pretty_devilish_file), dragon-themed crackme (UnholyDragon), NTFS forensics (ntfsm), extortion/demand chain (Chain of Demands), corporate espionage roleplay (The Boss Needs Help), mobile authenticator RE (FlareAuthenticator), and a massive 10000 iteration challenge (10000.7z at 1 GB). This corpus is used for forensic TTP classification and intentionality analysis training.

peirce_chain.firstness: ZIP archive (1.07 GB) containing 9 CTF challenge 7z files and PASSWORD.txt. Challenge names encode technique families: 'DrillBabyDrill' (disk drilling / forensic carving), 'ntfsm' (NTFS manipulation), 'Chain of Demands' (extortion/ransomware chain), 'FlareAuthenticator' (mobile 2FA reverse engineering), '10000' (iterative computational challenge requiring automation).
peirce_chain.secondness: Size distribution is diagnostic. 10000.7z at 1,010,655,700 bytes (97% of the ZIP) is anomalous — consistent with a challenge requiring a large pre-generated lookup table, a brute-force corpus, or a full disk image for carving. DrillBabyDrill at 14.5 MB suggests a disk image or memory dump for forensic challenge. Chain of Demands at 30.7 MB suggests a multi-file extortion simulation.
peirce_chain.thirdness: Each challenge encodes a deliberate adversarial or forensic technique. 'ntfsm' directly targets NTFS alternate data stream manipulation (T1564.004). 'Chain of Demands' encodes extortion mechanics (T1486 + T1657). 'FlareAuthenticator' targets mobile authentication bypass (T1521). The 10000 challenge name implies forced brute-force or symbolic execution at scale. The aggregate corpus is a curated training set for adversarial technique recognition.

devil_advocate: This is an authorized Mandiant/FLARE CTF educational corpus released for 2025. All samples are password-protected 7z archives. No attacker infrastructure is active. The challenges are sandboxed RE puzzles designed to teach defensive analysts adversarial techniques. Forensic interest is taxonomic and educational, not threat-response.
